title: Whether trust is an act of the intellect, and how it differs from assent
pass_a_gloss: Article XIX. Whether trust is an act of the intellect, and how it differs from assent. 1. The question is whether trust is in the intellect or in the will. The Papists commonly refer trust to the will. The Orthodox distinguish. 2. Trust, insofar as it is firm persuasion and judgment of the mind concerning God's promise, is an act of the intellect, and does not differ really from faith's assent, but in reason: assent regards the truth of the testimony; trust regards the goodness of the thing promised as applicable to me. 3. Trust, insofar as it is a loving motion toward God and the will's resting, is an act of the will, inseparable from faith in the justified, but formally distinct. 4. The middle Orthodox view: whole justifying faith is in the intellect as proper subject as to assent and persuasion; but it belongs to the will by reason of origin (commanded by the will), of concomitance (charity), and of fruits.
pass_b_english: Article XIX. Whether trust is an act of the intellect, and how it differs from assent.
1. Is trust in the intellect or the will? Papists commonly put it in the will. Orthodox distinguish.

2. As firm persuasion about God's promise, trust is an intellective act — not really distinct from faith's assent, but in reason: assent regards the testimony's truth; trust regards the promised good as applicable to me.
3. As loving motion and the will's resting on God, trust is a will-act — inseparable from faith in the justified, formally distinct.
4. Middle Orthodox view: justifying faith as assent and persuasion is in the intellect as proper subject; it belongs to the will by origin (will-commanded), concomitance (charity), and fruits.
source_text:
ART. XIX.
An fiducia sit actus intellectus, & quomodo differat ab assensu.

1. Quaeritur an fiducia sit in intellectu an in voluntate. Pontificii plerumque fiduciam ad voluntatem referunt. Orthodoxi distinguunt.

2. Fiducia, quatenus est firma persuasio & judicium mentis de DEI promissione, est actus intellectus, & non differt realiter ab assensu fidei, sed ratione: assensus respicit veritatem testimonii; fiducia respicit bonitatem rei promissae ut mihi applicabilis.

3. Fiducia, quatenus est amorosus in DEUM motus & recumbentia voluntatis, est actus voluntatis, a fide inseparabilis in justificato, sed formaliter distinctus.

4. Sententia Orthodоxa mediа: tota fides justificans est in intellectu tanquam in subjecto proprio quoad assensum & persuasionem; sed ad voluntatem pertinet ratione originis (a voluntate imperata), ratione concomitantiae (charitas), & ratione fructuum.
